privacy.intro: This policy says what {app} keeps about you, for how long, who processes it for us, and how you get a copy of it or have it deleted.

terms.intro: These terms apply when you use {app}. By using it, you agree to them.
terms.account: You sign in with a code we email you, or with a passkey. Keep your email account and your devices safe: whoever controls them can sign in as you.
terms.plans: A paid plan renews each period until you cancel it. You can cancel at any time in your settings, and keep the plan until the end of the period you paid for.
terms.merchant: {merchant} sells our plans and credits to you as merchant of record, and handles payment, taxes and invoices under its own terms.
terms.withdrawal: Where the law gives you a right to withdraw from a purchase, your settings show how while it applies.
terms.content: You keep the rights to what you create. You give us what we need to store it and show it to the people you share it with. Don't upload anything illegal, or anything that harms others.
terms.report: Report content that breaks the law or these terms. A person reviews every report, and the person whose content we restrict hears why and how to appeal.
terms.ai: Some features use AI models. What they make can be wrong, so check it before you rely on it.
terms.end: You can delete your account at any time. We may suspend an account that breaks these terms, and we tell you why.
terms.privacy: How we handle your data is in our privacy policy.
terms.changes: We tell you before a change to these terms takes effect.

accessibility.intro: We want everyone to be able to use {app}: with a keyboard, a screen reader, speech input or zoom.
accessibility.standard: We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at level AA, the web part of the European standard EN 301 549.
accessibility.check: The sign-in, account, billing and admin pages come from a toolkit built and tested against WCAG 2.2 levels A and AA, with a keyboard, a screen reader and an automated check in light and dark colors. We test the rest of the app ourselves.
accessibility.gaps: We know of no part of the app that falls short of the standard. If you find one, tell us.
accessibility.report: Tell us at {contact} what you tried to do and what stopped you, and we will answer.
accessibility.reportNoContact: Tell us what you tried to do and what stopped you, and we will answer.
accessibility.authority: If our answer does not solve it, you can contact the authority that enforces accessibility law where you live.

workspaces.holds: The workspaces an account belongs to, with its role in each, and the invitations it sent or was sent.
workspaces.kept: As long as the account; an unanswered invitation 30 days past its expiry.

auth.holds: The account: name, address, language, app role and ban, and whether it finished the first run and dismissed the activation checklist; its sessions with their browser and network address; its passkeys; the sign-in and email-change codes waiting for its address, stored as keyed hashes.
auth.kept: As long as the account; a session a day past its expiry, a code an hour past its expiry.

knownDevices.holds: The devices the account signed in from, for new-device alerts: a keyed hash of each device's browser, system and network range (never the fingerprint itself), the browser and system names, when it was first and last seen, and whether its first sign-in was alerted.
knownDevices.kept: A year after the device was last seen.

access.holds: The invitations by address an administrator made for the address, which ticket admitted the account while the app was closed (the redemption ledger), the codes and links it made as an administrator, and its waitlist entry: the address, its answers, its place and the state of its launch-news contact (the launch-news consent itself is on the consent ledger).
access.kept: An invitation by address until it is used or revoked; the ticket record as long as the account; a waitlist entry until the person leaves or is erased, and a join whose code never checked a day.

consents.holds: The consent ledger: one row for each time the account (or, before it signed up, a hash of its address) agreed to a document or an opt-in, withdrew it, or chose optional storage, with the kind, its version, the time and where it came from.
consents.kept: As long as the account; the rows of an address that never signed up until it is erased.

referrals.holds: The account's share code, the referral that brought it (when it claimed one), and the referrals it brought, as states and times: claimed, held, rewarded or voided. Never who the other person is, an order or an amount. The counters hold totals per referrer and month, and the program's by state; the tallies how many referrals and rewards each referrer has.

billing.holds: The cached plans, features and credit balances of the account's billing entities, their scheduled plan changes and quota keys, the save offers the cancel flow made them, and the trial the account used.
billing.kept: As long as the entity; a deletion mark 30 days.

billingProofs.holds: Proof of the consent to a renewing subscription (the plan, the price and interval shown, the terms version, when and by whom) and of each EU withdrawal: when and by whom.
billingProofs.kept: Three years; a checkout's proof that started no subscription two days.

gifts.holds: The gifts the account bought, with the address it sent each to and its message, and the gifts sent to its address.
gifts.kept: As long as the purchase is on the books.

billingCustomer.holds: The provider customer of each billing entity: its name, the owner's address, its members, payment method, orders and invoices.
billingCustomer.kept: The provider's own, for its tax and accounting duties.

billingSync.holds: The provider's customers and subscriptions as the billing component the app mounts syncs them: each billing entity's id beside its provider customer's, and each subscription's plan, price, dates and status, with the reason and comment of a cancellation.
billingSync.kept: Until that component can delete them.

rateLimits.holds: Better Auth's own limiter, off unless an app turns it on: a counter per route and network address.
rateLimits.kept: A day after its last request.

aiRequests.holds: The arguments of a metered AI stream the account started, while it runs.
aiRequests.kept: A day after it settles; a week if it never does.

jobs.holds: The generation jobs an account or its workspace queued (the job's arguments, who started it, its progress, result and cost), the budget each owner used per window, and how many guest tries the browser the account signed up in used, by its visitor cookie's id.
jobs.kept: Thirty days after a job ends, dead letters included; a budget window until its owner is erased; a browser's guest tries a year after its last, as long as the visitor cookie lasts.

aiCosts.holds: What each person's AI calls cost a day: the job queue's, metered actions, streams, chat replies and knowledge embeddings, in US dollars and tokens, with the billing entity that paid.

aiThreads.holds: The chat threads an account started: which chat and workspace each belongs to, its title and when it last changed. The messages live in the app's Agent component.
aiThreads.kept: Until the person deletes the thread, or the account or the workspace goes.

aiDocuments.holds: The knowledge documents an account added: their title, workspace and status. The passages and embeddings live in the app's RAG component.
aiDocuments.kept: Until a member removes it, or its workspace goes.

aiProvenance.holds: What made each generated image a workspace's jobs stored: the models, when, and the ids of the rows and files it was made from, never their content.
aiProvenance.kept: Until its workspace goes: the record is what shows an image was generated, for as long as the image is shown.

audit.holds: The account's activity: sign-ins, passkeys, email and session changes, workspace and billing events, as ids, never an address or a name.

notifications.holds: What the app told the account in its inbox: the kind of event, when, whether it was read and the workspace and thing it names, as ids, never the words, an address or a name; and the channels the account turned on or off for each kind.
notifications.kept: A read notification 90 days after it was read, an unread one 365 days after it was recorded; a channel choice until the account changes it.

pushSubscriptions.holds: Each device the account allowed web push on: the push service's address for it and the keys messages to it are encrypted with.
pushSubscriptions.kept: Until the push service says the device is gone, the account subscribes a newer one past twenty, or the device is subscribed by another account.

announcements.holds: Which announcements the account dismissed, and, for an administrator, the announcements they published or sent, by account id.
announcements.kept: An announcement and its dismissals 90 days after it expired.

lifecycle.holds: Each lifecycle email flow the account is in: which email, when it is due, its address, and whether it was sent, skipped by a sending rule or stopped.
lifecycle.kept: A finished run of a flow that may run again 90 days after it was due; the record of a flow sent once until the account is erased.

inbound.holds: The messages the account sent through the contact form, and the mail it (or its address) sent to the app: the sender's name and address, the subject, the text, the names and sizes of the attachments; and the reply addresses made for it, each a random token with the thread it answers.
inbound.kept: A message 90 days; a reply address a year after the last email it went out in.

reports.holds: The content the account reported in a click, and the notices sent from its address on the public form, with the notifier's name, address, language and typed signature. The decisions on content it wrote, with the text of its appeal. For an administrator, the decisions it made, the appeals it answered and the suspected crimes it flagged, by account id. The hashes of removed intimate images, which name no one.
reports.kept: A closed report or notice 548 days (18 months) after it was closed; a decision 548 days after it was made, with its appeal, once no appeal is open; a removed image's hash as long as the app keeps it.

flags.holds: The flags an administrator turned on for the account by its id.
flags.kept: Until an administrator changes the flag.

funnel.holds: How the growth funnel counts the account: its sign-up week, the invite, first campaign, referral code and promotion it came with, its answer to "How did you hear about us?" (with an "Other" answer's own words), the steps it reached and its last active week; and the experiments' variants it saw first.

email.holds: A code email waiting for the provider, and an email the person's quiet hours hold until they end.
email.kept: A code email until the provider answers, at most ten minutes; a held email until the quiet hours end.

emailRecords.holds: The emails sent to the address: recipients, subject, body and delivery status.
emailRecords.kept: 7 days after a final status, 30 days without one.

emailPreferences.holds: The address's choice for each email topic and how it was made, its time zone, when it last clicked an email or used the app, and when marketing mail went to it in the last 7 days.

emailContact.holds: The address as a contact of the email provider, with the segments and topics it is in.

suppressions.holds: The address, when the email provider stopped delivering to it after a hard bounce, a complaint or by hand: a copy of the provider's suppression list that sign-in reads before it sends a code.
suppressions.kept: While the provider suppresses the address; a week after it lifts the suppression.

files.holds: The files an account uploaded through setupStorage and the images its jobs generated, with their owner records (account, workspace, size, type) and quota counts, and the share links it turned on (the shared row, never the token).
files.kept: Until released by the app or erased; an upload nobody claimed a day.

exports.holds: The account's data exports, each a file behind a link, and the zip parts that bundle its files beside it.
exports.kept: The file an hour; its record a day, which the export limit counts.

deletions.holds: A deletion waiting out its grace period: the account's id, when it was asked for and when it runs, and a keyed hash of the token in the "keep my account" link.
deletions.kept: Until the deletion is cancelled or runs.

erasures.holds: An erasure in progress: the account's id and address, and the workspaces it deletes; and the plan of the app's part (the billing customer, the email contact) while a participant of it is retried.
erasures.kept: Until the erasure finishes; a failed one 30 days.

monitoringUser.holds: Error reports and cron check-ins with ids, never an address or a name. The package sets no user on a report.

deployment.processes: Everything the app stores: accounts, sessions, workspaces, billing state, email records, uploaded files, exports and logs.
deployment.location: The region the deployment was created in: the US, the EU (Dublin), Canada or Australia.

host.processes: Each request to the app, with its network address and browser. On another host, that host instead.
host.location: The functions region the app is deployed to; Vercel is a US company.

billing.processes: The customer of each paying account or workspace: name, email address, billing address, payment method, orders, subscriptions and invoices. As merchant of record it sells to customers in its own name, under its own terms.
billing.location: The US, Canada or elsewhere outside the EEA and the UK.

email.processes: The emails the app sends, their delivery events, and the contacts and topics people subscribe to.
email.location: The US; mail leaves from the sending domain's region.

botCheck.processes: Signals of the browser and the request (network address, browser, TLS fingerprint) when someone signs in, signs up or sends a protected form, to tell people from bots.
botCheck.location: The US, and the provider's network worldwide.

webPush.processes: The notifications sent to a device a person turned them on for: the device's push address, and each message, encrypted so the service reads only where and when it goes.
webPush.location: Each browser maker's own network, mostly in the US.

aiGateway.processes: The prompts and the answers of the AI features a person uses, which the gateway passes to the model's provider; never kept by the app past the request.
aiGateway.location: The US, or the EU where inference is pinned there.

monitoring.processes: Error reports and cron check-ins, scrubbed of addresses, names and credentials, with an account's id at most; a masked session replay only after the person allowed it.
monitoring.location: The US or the EU, as the organization was created.

consents.necessary: Not asked: the app needs it
consents.replay: Only once you allow session replay

session.lasts: 7 days, renewed while they use the app.

sessionJwt.why: Proves to the backend who is signed in, for the pages the server renders.

signInCode.why: Makes the code work only in the browser that asked for it.

passkeyChallenge.why: Holds the challenge the passkey answers.

underAge.why: Keeps a second answer from following at once.

impersonation.why: Returns the administrator to their own session when the visit ends.

storageChoice.why: Remembers what they allowed, so nothing optional is stored unasked.
storageChoice.lasts: 6 months, then the prompt asks again.

lastSignIn.why: Marks the way they signed in last, so the sign-in form can suggest it.

visitor.why: Counts what this browser did before signing up, and hands it to the account made here.

invite.why: Keeps the invite until the sign-in that uses it.

presence.why: Tells the backend their time zone at most once a day, so emails respect their quiet hours.

upgradeDismissed.why: Keeps the prompt hidden for the time the app sets. Without preferences allowed, it is kept for the tab only.
upgradeDismissed.lasts: The app's cool-down, a year at most.

pushSubscription.why: The push subscription lets the app send that device notifications. The service worker, where the browser needs one, shows them and opens the app on a click; it caches nothing.
pushSubscription.lasts: Until the person turns notifications off on the device or takes back the site's permission.

replay.why: Records, masked, the minute before an error and the rest of that visit, to find what went wrong.
